title: The Human Aura: Astral Colors and Thought Forms
author: Swami Panchadasi (pseudonym of William Walker Atkinson)
edition_cited: Project Gutenberg ebook #22739 (text of the 1912 Yoga Publication Society edition)
tradition: American New Thought occultism (pseudo-Indian persona, non-lineage)
locator_hints: Chapter II, 'The Prana-Aura': the hand against a black background in dim light with narrowed eyelids; heat-shimmer comparison
Later chapters on developing the aura by visualising colours (imaginal, probably out of scope)
summary: A short popular manual. The relevant passage is in Chapter II: the 'prana-aura' is said to be visible to trained ordinary sight, not clairvoyance. The reader places a hand against a black background in dim light and gazes with narrowed eyelids, squinting if necessary; after a little practice a thin outline or halo of pale yellowish light appears round the hand and round each spread finger, compared to the radiance round a candle flame and, at best, almost phosphorescent. It is also likened to the vibrating air above a hot stove. The remaining chapters assign meanings to colours seen by clairvoyants and teach colour visualisation, without a method for seeing them.
why_relevant: A plain, early statement of the standard aura-seeing exercise (dark ground, dim light, narrowed lids), useful for judging whether such exercises are contrast and afterimage effects; the author himself calls it ordinary sight.

date_evidence.basis: archive.org record human_aura_panchadasi gives 1912; Gutenberg text of that edition

author_basis: William Walker Atkinson (1862-1932) writing as Swami Panchadasi
found_via: seed lead (aura-seeing exercises); archive.org creator search
notes: May overlap with the western-esoteric stream; only one passage is practical for seen light.
